note: Every byte below is derived from fixed labels; regenerate with the generator, never by hand. Hex is lower-case throughout.

constants.challenge_layout: nonce(16) || HMAC-SHA256(relay_secret, challenge_domain || identity_hash(16) || u64be(registration_seq) || nonce(16))

A.description: the relay every vector is presented to; it lists the gateway identity in [registration] transit_identities

B.description: another relay; its challenges and its audience must be refused at A

lowx.note: X25519 half is the all-zero (low-order) point: the Ed25519 signature verifies, but no session token can be encrypted to it.

registrations.description: Retichat-js browser, first signed registration at relay A: no signed row exists for the identity, so the challenge's MAC binds seq 0 and the relay INSERTs.

The same browser re-registering after a 401 (session lost): its row is at seq 1, so the challenge's MAC binds seq 1 and the relay UPDATEs the row in place to seq 2. The name carries non-ASCII characters to pin UTF-8.

Reticulum-rust gateway (or Python PostInterface) in wake mode, signing with its persistent transport identity, which relay A lists in transit_identities: client reticulum-php, mode 6, with peer_url / peer_interface_id / peer_session_token covered by the signature. Its row is at seq 5.
The same gateway identity in poll mode (no wake_url): client rns-post-interface with the transport field, no peer fields (signed as empty strings). First registration, seq 0.

negative.description: browser-first with the name changed after signing.
browser-first with bitrate changed after signing.
gateway-wake with peer_url changed after signing.
gateway-wake with peer_session_token changed after signing.
browser-first's exact signed bytes, signed by a different identity, presented with the browser's public key.
browser-first replayed verbatim after it succeeded. The signature is valid, but the row is now at seq 1 and the challenge's MAC bound seq 0.
A correctly signed gateway registration over a challenge relay A issued while the row was at seq 4, presented after the row moved to seq 5.
A correctly signed browser registration, addressed to relay A, over a challenge minted by relay B (different relay_secret). Same identity, same seq: only the MAC differs.
The browser signs (validly) a challenge relay A issued for another identity. The MAC covers the identity hash, so it fails for the browser's hash.
The browser flips one bit of the nonce inside a real seq-0 challenge and signs the result validly. The MAC no longer matches: a client cannot alter a challenge.

A correctly signed browser registration over a real relay-A challenge, but the browser connected to relay B (audience relay-b.example.org) and relay B forwarded the body to A: the relay-oracle attack. A refuses an audience that is not its own host.
browser-first plus metadata.identity_hash naming another identity (not a signed field, so the signature still verifies).
browser-first plus metadata.wake_url, a key the signature does not cover.
browser-first with the public key in upper-case hex. Hex fields are lower-case only.
A correctly signed rns-js registration with mode 6 (gateway). Browsers are endpoints: modes 3, 5 and 6 are refused for client rns-js.
A correctly signed rns-js registration that names a peer_url. A browser row may not carry peer fields: they would make it look like a PHP peer and draw wakes to any URL.
A correctly signed registration with client "x". Only rns-js, reticulum-php and rns-post-interface may register signed.
The listed gateway, correctly signed, client reticulum-php with no peer fields. A wake-mode gateway must name where it is woken.
The listed gateway, correctly signed, client rns-post-interface carrying a peer_url. A poll-mode gateway is never woken, so it may not name a URL.
A correctly signed wake-mode gateway registration by an identity relay A does not list in transit_identities. Anyone can make a key; only listed identities get a transit row.
A correctly signed first registration (a new row) while relay A's interfaces table is at max_interface_rows and nothing is reclaimable.

A correctly signed browser registration whose public key has the all-zero (low-order) X25519 half. The Ed25519 signature verifies, but no token can be encrypted to the key, so the relay refuses it before writing anything.

tokens_negative.description: browser-first's encrypted token with one ciphertext bit flipped: the HMAC fails, decryption must fail, the client must not use it.
browser-first's encrypted token decrypted by the gateway identity: a token is readable only by the identity it was encrypted to.

url_canonical.note: host lower-cased, trailing slash dropped; the path keeps its case
scheme lower-cased, default port and /v1/wake dropped
path case is significant: a different key
an IDN look-alike in ASCII form: valid, and a different key
a non-ASCII look-alike: refused, never folded onto retichat.com
